Brihadisvara Temple

A thousand years of granite

Rajaraja Chola completed it in 1010 CE, and it has stood through every century since.

Photo: Lux@Photography (CC BY 2.0)

The vimana above the sanctum rises about sixty-six metres, and it was built without mortar, from granite that had to be brought from far outside the delta. The inscriptions around the base are the reason historians know so much about Chola administration: they list the dancers, musicians, accountants and oil suppliers the temple employed, by name. It is a cathedral and a civil service record in the same building.

About this route

Thanjavur holds the Brihadisvara temple, the Maratha palace that came after the Cholas, and one of the oldest working libraries in Asia, all within a short walk. This route moves from the temple's granite vimana to the palace quarter, taking in the art gallery's Chola bronzes on the way.
